# 1.1.0 — health, retention, and private media

The fleet can say whether an instance is actually connected, old rows and
unreferenced media can expire, and stored files are private unless you opt in.
**Read the upgrade notes first:** migrations run on start, and the global S3
bucket is no longer public.

## Upgrade notes

Migrations `0016` and `0017` run on start. `0016` adds `audit_logs`. `0017`
adds an index for searching every conversation of an instance.

- **The global S3/MinIO bucket is private.** It no longer receives a public
  `s3:GetObject` policy unless `S3_PUBLIC_READ=true`. Media URLs are presigned.
  A per-instance `publicUrl` is still an explicit public-read signal.
- **Webhook, Typebot and per-instance S3 URLs are SSRF-guarded.** Loopback,
  private, link-local and CGNAT destinations need
  `INTEGRATIONS_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true`.
- **`WEBHOOK_INCLUDE_TOKEN` stays `true`.** Set it to `false` to drop
  `instanceToken` from webhook, RabbitMQ, NATS and WebSocket payloads.
  `instanceId` and `instanceName` remain.
- **A push to `main` publishes a pre-release.** The version tag is pushed and
  `latest` is left where it is. **Actions → Promote release** points `latest`
  and `1.1` at that image and marks the GitHub Release as latest.

## Health and reconnects

- `/instance/status`, `/instance/inventory` and `/metrics` report a verdict
  (`ok`, `reconnecting`, `looping`, `stalled`, `closed`) from the last event,
  inbound message and ack. Nothing is written to the database.
- `WATCHDOG_MODE` defaults to `report`. `on` rebuilds one socket whose state
  says open but whose websocket is closed, and stops after
  `WATCHDOG_MAX_REBUILDS`. It never logs out.
- A 440 loop no longer resets its budget on the brief `Connected` that each
  attempt produces. Logged out, banned, primary-device-gone and replaced
  sessions stop reconnecting; the session stays for a manual connect.
  `RECONNECT_CONFLICT_LIMIT` defaults to 10.
- `INSTANCE_IDLE_EVICT_MINUTES` defaults to `0` (off). When set, a disconnected
  instance's in-memory client is dropped after the window. The row, JID and
  session stay.

## Retention and search

- Message retention deletes an object in the global bucket only when no
  remaining row still references it. Per-instance buckets are not pruned.
- `send_operations` expire after 30 days by default. `chat_reads`,
  `chat_states`, `typebot_sessions` and `poll_votes` have their own knobs;
  `0` keeps a table.
- `GET /chat/history/search` accepts `q` without `chat` and searches every
  conversation of the instance.
- One bad history row no longer drops the batch. `HISTORY_SYNC_DAYS`,
  `HISTORY_SYNC_MAX_MB` and `HISTORY_STORAGE_QUOTA_MB` replace the fixed
  limits (defaults: 3650 days, 10 GB, 10 GB).

## Also

- A `played` receipt is stored as `Played`, above `Read`. The manager shows it.
- `POST /ws/ticket` with an instance token subscribes that socket only to its
  instance. A global key still opens any stream.
- `GET /server/audit` (admin key) lists create, delete, rename, proxy, S3,
  HMAC, settings and token-read events. The detail object has no secrets.
- Instance settings can edit per-instance S3 and webhook HMAC, and show the
  health verdict.
- `/instance/all` no longer writes an audit row per request. A 1,000-request
  run went from about 624 to about 1,277 req/s.
